brief.title: Keep JSON store or move to SQLite?
brief.question: Should BenchMemo keep file-backed persistence for the next milestone, or move to SQLite now when rollback risk is material?

options.name: Keep file-backed persistence
options.description: Retain the current store until rollback risk is better understood.

options.name: Move to SQLite now
options.description: Adopt SQLite immediately despite the rollback surface.

constraints: Rollback risk is a primary concern

frame.normalizedQuestion: Should BenchMemo keep file-backed persistence for the next milestone, or move to SQLite now when rollback risk is material?

options.name: Keep file-backed persistence
options.description: Retain the current store until rollback risk is better understood.

options.description: Adopt SQLite immediately despite the rollback surface.

criteria.name: Risk
criteria.scoringGuidance: Prefer the option with the lower rollback and migration blast radius.

criteria.name: Velocity
criteria.scoringGuidance: Prefer the option that avoids introducing urgent migration work.

opt_file.summary: Keep the reversible path for now.

claims.text: Keeping the current store minimizes rollback risk this milestone.
claims.rationale: The current path avoids format migration and downgrade handling.

opt_sqlite.summary: SQLite could still improve durability later.

claims.text: SQLite could reduce persistence correctness risk over time.
claims.rationale: A database-backed store may help once the product matures.

opt_file.summary: Staying put can delay real improvements.

claims.text: Keeping the current store delays richer persistence capabilities.
claims.rationale: Eventually the team may need a database-backed store.

claims.text: SQLite introduces rollback-risk because persistence format and downgrade handling would change.
claims.rationale: The repo would need migration safety and reverse compatibility work.

repoProbes.summary: Keeping the current store avoids a format migration and preserves the current downgrade path.
The current path keeps rollback-risk contained for the milestone.
SQLite would require migration tooling, downgrade behavior, and updated tests.
Rollback risk is materially higher for SQLite because migration and downgrade behavior would need to be correct immediately.
operationalRisks: A broken migration could strand existing decision data.

evidenceItems.title: Current store preserves the existing rollback path
evidenceItems.excerpt: Keeping the current store avoids changing persistence format during a hard-to-reverse window.

evidenceItems.title: SQLite migration expands rollback risk
evidenceItems.excerpt: A SQLite move would require migration tooling and downgrade handling during a hard-to-reverse period.

claimStatuses.notes: Keeping the store minimizes rollback-risk this milestone.
The rollback surface makes SQLite the riskier short-term move.
The current store is not the immediate rollback threat.
Rollback risk is materially higher for SQLite right now.

judgeDraft.executiveSummary: Keep file-backed persistence for the next milestone because rollback risk is materially lower than a SQLite migration in a hard-to-reverse window.

criterionScores.rationale: Keeping the store preserves the current rollback path.
It also avoids migration work during the milestone.
Rollback-risk is materially higher because migration and downgrade behavior would need to be correct immediately.
SQLite would add migration work during a short horizon.

keyRisks: SQLite would make rollback behavior a first-class delivery risk right away.
dissent: If rollback constraints ease later, SQLite could become more attractive.
nextSteps: Document rollback expectations before reconsidering a persistence migration.
